reasoning_content:
No Gradle lockfile in backend. No reference to maven.pkg.github.com anywhere in the build scripts. The GITHUB_TOKEN is passed as a build secret, but the token is only consumed if the convention plugin actually uses it to authenticate to a GitHub Packages repository. I've confirmed that `githubPackagesToken` is defined in RepoAuthKt but is not referenced from other classes. Let me re-check by looking at which classes reference the method `githubPackagesToken` — the reference might be via method descriptor rather than FQN. Let me search for the "RepoAuthKt" string in constant pools of all classes.

Actually, my rawsearch.js searched for the "RepoAuth" byte sequence in all .class files and found only RepoAuthKt.class itself. If another class were calling RepoAuthKt.githubPackagesToken, the constant pool would contain "io/swcode/urbo/build/logic/RepoAuthKt" (the class name) — my search should have caught that. Nothing else references it. So this helper function is actually dead code, or possibly called via reflection or from a Gradle script that isn't in this jar.

Wait — actually, it's also possible the token is used in settings.gradle.kts's pluginManagement or the project's build.gradle.kts... but I've already confirmed there are no repository definitions using the token in the repo files.

So the most likely scenario is this: the GITHUB_TOKEN requirement is a defensive check ("pulling packages from GitHub"), but for this particular commit, all dependencies resolve from public registries (S3 urbo-maven, Maven Central, Gradle Plugin Portal). The token is passed as a Docker build secret, but if no repository requires authentication, the build will succeed with any non-empty value.

The empirical test will confirm: the build is currently running `./gradlew bootJar` with a dummy token.
